topics.title: Appendix C — Numerical Verification for Signal Processing
topics.summary: Begin with analytically simple fixtures. An impulse exposes indexing and convolution alignment. A constant sequence exposes gain and DC behavior. A single complex tone exposes frequency-bin mapping and sign conventions. Small hand-computable vectors make correlation and convolution boundaries inspectable. Random inputs are valuable later but are weak first diagnostics because the expected answer is difficult to reason about manually.

blocks.text: For FFT libraries, record transform direction, normalization convention, data layout, batch dimensions, strides, and overwrite behavior. Compare CPU and GPU implementations under the same convention. A constant scaling difference may indicate normalization rather than a broken transform, but it still violates the interface if normalized output was promised.
